doc.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Live-recorded sessions at Enja and Capitol
summary: Enja's producer wants mistakes; Cannonball's live Capitol contract; the Harlem Lullaby date was live.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: That’s right. Yeah. But this producer at Enja, he says, “I want mistakes and all.” He says that’s jazz. And the only time he’ll take a second take is like if somebody in the booth messes up, or if the tape runs out or something. But other than that, it’s like recording live. Now when Cannonball signed with Capitol Records, he made a deal with them, or he had it put in his contract, that all of his sessions were going to be live, which if you notice most of the Capitol sessions are. I think this was after, one of the last Riverside

things he did was a live date, and that was the biggest hit he had. And so everything after that was done live. The last date I did for Enja, that’s the one we did “Harlem Lullaby” on, that’s live. And there’s a difference too. You know, you’ve got a different set of emotions when you’re playing live.
